basis: Cerebellar dysfunction, intellectual disability and gonadotropin deficiency define the syndrome; scoliosis affects 3/3 patients.
Cerebral small-vessel disease causes hemorrhage, porencephaly and developmental brain injury; esotropia alone does not establish direct ocular damage.
Defining abnormalities affect teeth, hair and nails, and the bones of the hands and feet.
Benign sweat-gland epithelial neoplasm arising in the dermis.
Tumour originates in the Skene paraurethral gland, classified here as a vulvar gland; urethral invasion is not established as a defining or common feature.
Nodular degeneration directly affects the cornea.
Hereditary corticospinal disease with frequent developmental impairment, abnormal myelination and peripheral neuropathy.
Acute pharyngeal inflammation, usually caused by viral or bacterial infection; pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Menstrual absence is a reproductive disorder; this umbrella does not establish an endocrine cause.
Developmental disability, macrodontia and skeletal anomalies define KBG; conductive hearing loss occurs in 30-79%. Ocular findings omitted under the four-axis cap.
Middle-ear inflammation caused by pathological type I hypersensitivity.
Mucinous adenocarcinoma originates in the urinary bladder.
Absence of the tibia and congenital hearing loss are the defining abnormalities.
Mitochondrial metabolic failure with encephalomyopathy defines the group; sensorineural hearing loss is a characteristic defining feature. Renal dysfunction is variable.
Inherited heme-synthesis defect with characteristic neonatal hemolytic anemia; photosensitivity frequency is uncertain. Hemolytic jaundice alone does not establish liver injury.
POMT2-related skeletal muscular dystrophy; cognitive and learning impairment occur in 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy and ventricular dysfunction occur in only 5-29%.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Defining cortical and other brain malformations; optic nerve hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%. Strabismus alone does not establish direct ocular injury.
Intellectual disability and primary testicular hormone failure define the syndrome; craniosynostosis and delayed skeletal maturation occur in 80-99%.
Localized cutaneous mucin deposition produces persistent papules; no systemic organ involvement is established.
Congenital intestinal sodium-transport dysfunction causes severe diarrhea with defining hyponatremia and metabolic acidosis.
ZIC2-related forebrain malformation; hypothalamic dysfunction with central diabetes insipidus affects roughly half or more of HPE patients, though subtype frequency is uncertain.
Melanoma originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; melanocytic histology does not imply skin involvement.
Broad infectious umbrella; vascular, blood-cell and other organ involvement varies by pathogen and is not established across most of the group.
Inherited neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; muscle-fiber atrophy and arthrogryposis occur in 30-79%. Respiratory and bulbar weakness do not establish lung or gut injury.
